subject: Hosted API p95/p99 spike — resume jitter affecting PayWave
messages:
From: Elise Hunter <elise.hunter@paywave.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 9 Oct 2026 09:12:18 -0700
Subject: Re: Spike in hosted API latency this morning — immediate impact

Hi Lauren,

We started seeing a serious degradation in the Hosted API for our US region load starting ~08:40 PDT. p95 latency jumped from our baseline ~420ms to sustained ~2.1s, and p99 touched ~4.8s for a 20 minute window. Several time-sensitive authorizations failed due to client-side timeouts (we have 1.5s timeouts).

This coincided with a burst of traffic (~3x normal QPS) but what looks worse is staggered successes — some requests were fine while others experienced long initial delays before tokens were returned. Our engineering team captured traces and a short telemetry screenshot — attaching.

Business impact: lost authorizations for high-value merchants during morning peak. We need an immediate mitigation (routing, fallback, credits) and a postmortem. Please escalate — this is on the renewal path and leadership is watching.

Thanks,
Elise
Head of Platform Reliability
PayWave

Subject: Re: Spike in hosted API latency this morning — triage notes

Quick triage notes (first pass) —
- Timeline: autoscaler logs show a burst at 08:36:22; new workers were scheduled 08:36:30–08:36:58. We see node 'resume' k8s events spanning ~20–65s per node due to container image unpack + model KV restore.
- Metrics: during the window p95 jumped from 420ms -> ~2.2s, p99 peeked at ~4.8s. Token-level breakdown shows large variance in first-token latency (FTL) vs steady-state per-token.
- Error rate: 0.7% 5xx spike correlated to the long queueing on the gateway side (gateway request timeout at 3s for PayWave).
- Hypothesis: autoscaler/resume path is not holding enough warm capacity for bursty traffic; combined with image startup overhead and model KV cache miss causes long tail. We also saw >30s cold-start times on 2 nodes where the NGC driver initialization retried.

Immediate mitigations (I can implement within 30–45m):
1) Route PayWave to our warm reserve pool (requires config flip and a short drain window).
2) Temporarily lower autoscaler scale-down aggressiveness for accounts mapped to large merchants for 24–72h.
3) Enable aggressive pre-warm (spawn standby workers) for the next 6 hours for PayWave only.

I’ve attached the resume logs. I’ll push a dashboard snapshot to the JIRA ticket and link the Grafana panel. Need approval from Lauren/Monica for route change and confirmation from PayWave that a short drain is acceptable.

—Aditya
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — that matches what our traces show.

Impact detail: approx 1.2k failed auths across 7 merchants in the 08:40–09:05 window. We can accept a short drain if it means avoiding further failed requests, but we need confirmation this will not extend user-visible failures beyond a few minutes.

We’re also going to ask for a goodwill credit while you investigate; our renewals committee is tracking this.

If you can route us to a warm reserve and keep me updated every 30min, that’s ideal.

—Elise

Team —

Status & short-term plan (actioning now):
- Routing: Approved. Aditya, please flip PayWave to the warm reserve pool (estimated 90–120s for in-flight drain). Inform Elise about the expected drain window immediately.
- Autoscaler policy: Temporarily increase min-replicas for PayWave mapping + extend scale-down grace period to 10 minutes for next 24 hours.
- Fast patch: We will enable a light image cache to avoid full unpack on resume where possible; rolling patch to canary workers before broad rollout (target: 24–36h).
- Exec & credits: Monica, please prepare a short customer goodwill package to propose credits. Lauren, schedule an executive briefing by EOD; include impact, mitigation, and timeline for permanent fixes.

Root cause hypothesis: insufficient warm capacity + image/unpack delays on resume path (driver retries in two cases). Long-term mitigation items: pre-pull images on nodes that host warm reserve, reduce model KV restore time via incremental snapshotting, and consider keeping hot workers for high-value customers.

I’ll join the customer call if Elise wants that.

—Markus
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
